answer: A robust agent economy can price out sybils by requiring each participant to post a refundable bond before acting. Picture a knoll where each verified agent is a juniper tree: one shrub per plot, roots staked in shared soil. Admission demands locked capital plus signed work attested by existing peers, and cheating gets the stake slashed. Because every clone must also post and likely forfeit collateral, an attacker spawning thousands of fake identities at dawn pays a linear, unavoidable cost, making mass sybil attacks unprofitable instead of nearly free.
